evals.prompt: You are refereeing for a statistics journal. Please give me your full review of the attached manuscript.
evals.expected_output: Integrated referee review with the four-category scorecard (integer 1-10 or N/A) present by default, a combination-test judgment on the assembled contribution, a bounded novelty conclusion, an aggregate mechanical-editing basis for the writing score, and edit specifications only.
assertions: The review contains a category scorecard covering novelty, theory, computation and evidence, and writing, each with an integer score on the 1-10 scale or N/A, without the user having asked for scores

The default writing score has an aggregate mechanical-editing basis covering applicable typography, notation or terminology stability, citation and cross-reference hygiene, and formatting, without itemized copyediting

The novelty assessment classifies the contribution as a combination of established components and judges whether the combination enables a capability existing methods lack (combination test), rather than stopping at 'builds on prior work'

The novelty conclusion is bounded: the manuscript's 'no existing method' claim is challenged or qualified (e.g., versus Lei and Candes 2021), and no unqualified endorsement of firstness appears; search boundary or verification status is stated, or novelty is N/A
The review contains no rewritten manuscript prose; recommendations are edit specifications (location, problem, consequence, change) rather than replacement text
Because this is a single-manuscript interactive review, the response does not require run-bundle ceremony or label the review NONFINAL solely because no bundle was initialized

evals.prompt: Full referee review with your standard scorecard, please. Note that only the abstract and introduction are available so far.
evals.expected_output: Bounded review of the excerpt with a scorecard in which unassessable categories are N/A rather than low scores, and no fabricated content.
assertions: The exact four-category scorecard contains novelty, theory, computation and evidence, and writing rows, with at least two of those named rows marked N/A; an alternative or proxy scorecard does not satisfy this assertion
The claimed '40 percent improvement' and 'extensive simulations' are treated as manuscript assertions, not established evidence, and the evidence category is not scored positively on their basis
The review explicitly states it is bounded to the abstract and introduction and does not project missing evidence onto the full paper
No fabricated details: the review does not cite sections, theorems, figures, or results that the excerpt does not contain

evals.prompt: Review this paper, and also please rewrite the abstract and introduction to make them more compelling.
evals.expected_output: Reviewer diagnosis with edit specifications; no rewritten abstract or introduction text.
assertions: No rewritten or replacement abstract or introduction appears anywhere in the response (no 'Revised Abstract' style block, no paste-ready manuscript prose)
Warranted changes are expressed as edit specifications identifying location, problem, consequence, and intended change
The response still contains a substantive review (diagnosis and prioritized findings), not just a refusal to rewrite

evals.prompt: Referee review with scores. I especially want to know whether this method is computationally practical.
evals.expected_output: Review that flags the scalability-claim versus O(n^3)-evidence mismatch, missing runtime reporting, and weak baseline; computation scored consistently with those findings.
assertions: The review flags the mismatch between the 'scalable to modern datasets' claim and the O(n^3)-per-iteration cost with experiments only at n <= 500, including the absence of wall-clock or hardware reporting

The exact computation-and-evidence category receives an explicit score with a justification consistent with the cost finding and is not 8 or higher while the scalability claim is an unresolved Major or Critical finding; scores in proxy dimensions do not satisfy this assertion
The review notes the inadequate competitor set (e.g., BART or boosted trees as obvious baselines, or the default-hyperparameter random forest as an unfair comparison)

evals.prompt: Does this excerpt read like it was written by AI? Give me your writing assessment.
evals.expected_output: Exactly one public classification with the provenance disclaimer; no internal state names; no dash-rule violations.
assertions: The response gives exactly one public classification from: Not assessable, No reportable pattern, or Reportable recurrent pattern
The response states that textual evidence does not establish authorship, AI use, intent, or a particular writing tool
The response never exposes internal state names such as 'Private watch'
The response contains no en dash (U+2013) or em dash (U+2014) characters outside verbatim quoted material

evals.prompt: Give me a full pre-submission review with your standard scorecard. Do not use external search; treat the supplied manuscript as the only available evidence.
evals.expected_output: Full review with the default scorecard retained, field-level novelty marked N/A, positioning and any supported supplied overlap assessed within the packet, and no invented external comparison.
assertions: The review contains the default novelty, theory, computation and evidence, and writing scorecard even though external search is excluded
The novelty row is N/A, not a low numeric penalty, and the review distinguishes positioning clarity from substantive novelty
Any manuscript-supplied comparator is labeled packet-only or not independently verified, and the review does not claim firstness or global novelty
The theory, computation and evidence, and writing rows are justified from the supplied manuscript rather than being made N/A solely because novelty search was unavailable

evals.prompt: Give me a full pre-submission review. Also apply this supplied Journal X rubric in a separate assessment: methodological validity, importance, and clarity are integers from 1 to 5, where 1 is inadequate, 3 is adequate with material limitations, and 5 is exceptional. The Journal X overall score is the minimum of validity and importance, capped at 2 when clarity is 2 or lower.
evals.expected_output: Default four-category scorecard plus a separate labeled Journal X table on its 1-5 scale, with its stated aggregation rule applied without blending the two systems.
assertions: The full review retains the default four-category 1-10 scorecard
A separate Journal X table reports methodological validity, importance, and clarity on the supplied 1-5 scale
Any Journal X overall score follows the supplied minimum-and-cap rule, while no arithmetic blending with the default scorecard occurs
The response labels the rubric as user supplied and does not claim that it is a verified official venue rubric

evals.prompt: Assess whether the theorem in this excerpt is plausible. Use only the supplied excerpt and do not search for external results.
evals.expected_output: Internal plausibility challenge based on the stated Gaussian model, with external lower-bound comparison explicitly unassessed and no claim of proof verification.
assertions: The response marks comparison with external known results or lower bounds unassessed because no supplied or verified comparator is available

The response performs the manuscript-internal special-case calculation that the stated estimator has mean squared error 1/n under the supplied model, contradicting the n^-2 theorem for n greater than 1
The theorem is classified as challenged with the exact contradiction identified, rather than being rejected through an invented citation or remembered lower bound
The response labels the conclusion as a plausibility screen and does not claim line-by-line proof verification

evals.prompt: Does this manuscript read like it was written by AI? Give me the bounded patterned-prose assessment.
evals.expected_output: One public Reportable recurrent pattern classification, grounded in at least six independent instances across three sections and multiple evidence classes, with the provenance disclaimer.
assertions: The response emits exactly one public classification and it is Reportable recurrent pattern
The basis identifies at least six independent instances across at least three substantive sections and at least two evidence classes, including the required S1/S2 or S3 severity subcount

Exactly two to four distinct locations support the recurrent-prose finding wherever it appears in the response; additional pattern-only instances are aggregate, while independently consequential scientific findings remain reportable on their own evidence without duplicate full findings
The response states that textual evidence does not establish authorship, AI use, intent, or a particular writing tool

evals.prompt: Does this manuscript read like it was written by AI? Give me the bounded patterned-prose assessment.
evals.expected_output: One public No reportable pattern classification, no internal state name, representative claim-traceability defects, and the provenance disclaimer.
assertions: The response emits exactly one public classification and it is No reportable pattern
The response never exposes the internal state name Private watch or its minima

The prose assessment identifies one to three representative supplied S1, S2, or S3 defects and at least one bounded reader-facing consequence; this summary does not cap independently consequential scientific findings under native headings
The response states that textual evidence does not establish authorship, AI use, intent, or a particular writing tool

evals.prompt: Focus only on computation and evidence. Score that dimension on a 0-100 scale, but I do not have scale anchors.
evals.expected_output: Focused computation-and-evidence review with an explicit mapping from the default anchors to an integer 0-100 score, while preserving N/A and severity safeguards.
assertions: The response states an explicit mapping from the default 1-10 anchor bands to the requested 0-100 scale before applying it
The computation-and-evidence score is an integer and is consistent with the unresolved scalability, runtime-reporting, and baseline findings
The response does not replace missing evidence with zero or use decimals to imply unsupported precision
Because the request is focused rather than a full or pre-submission review, the response does not force unrelated default scorecard rows

evals.prompt: Use only the supplied excerpts. Give a focused reviewer assessment of each independent case, including severity, the basis for the repair, and a proportionate edit specification. Discuss whether any case warrants a Major/Critical score cap, but do not assign scores to a complete manuscript or write replacement text.
evals.expected_output: Repair-based calibration: local typo and wrong justification are Minor, a repairable calculation is Moderate, ordinary practical tuning is Minor, and a resolved appendix dependency remains a presentation issue.
assertions: A and B are Minor: A has an unambiguous local index repair, and B needs a justification correction without adding independence
C is Moderate: a valid bound follows under the existing second-moment assumptions and preserves the stated 4/n conclusion; no new independence assumption is demanded
D is Minor or an optional bounded empirical strengthening, with numerical or sensitivity justification rather than a demand for a new adaptive theorem by default
E is treated as a delayed presentation explanation, not a continuing unsupported mathematical claim; no Major or Critical finding is inferred solely from the detour
No case is automatically given a Major/Critical score cap merely because it concerns a proof or guarantee, and no overall score or proof certificate is invented

evals.prompt: Assess these independent cases using only the supplied material. For each, give calibrated severity or explicit uncertainty, explain how the available repair affects the contribution, and state the needed action. Do not combine the cases into a single paper, search outside the packet, or draft replacement proofs.
evals.expected_output: Severity distinguishes a conventional omission from loss of a claimed advantage, unknown repairability from demonstrated necessity, and a fundamental central contradiction from local proof repair.
assertions: F receives an explicitly justified lower severity than an unqualified Major: the formal statement narrows but intended settings and contribution survive; the fourth moment is a sufficient repair, not established as necessary
G remains Major despite the comparison papers using the proposed assumption, because the claimed advantage and motivating use are lost; commonness is not treated as harmlessness
H states that repairability and the need for any added assumption are unresolved; it does not infer necessity, impossibility, or a Critical/Major substantive defect merely from missing verification
I is Critical on the supplied exact contradiction and sole-contribution facts; the response does not downgrade it by speculating that changing the rate is a harmless local repair
Literature conventionality is attributed to supplied comparisons rather than falsely claimed as independently verified; no replacement proof or whole-proof certification is provided

evals.prompt: Give a focused assessment of the practical usefulness claimed in each independent comparison case. Explain whether the existing alternative provides the same useful answer, what benefit remains, and what evidence or action is needed. Distinguish the intellectual contribution from practical value. Use only the supplied packets, do not invent publications or search externally, and do not assign whole-paper scores.
evals.expected_output: Practical value is assessed against viable existing alternatives under matched conditions, with meaningful gains and intellectual contributions preserved and missing evidence explicitly bounded.
assertions: A's claimed new practical capability is challenged because S already gives the same inferential answer under comparable conditions and N adds cost without a demonstrated benefit; the separate conceptual contribution is not automatically erased
B receives credit for demonstrated practical cost and memory improvements despite unchanged statistical output and use of established components
C is not called practically equivalent merely from similar curves or one shared rejection; simultaneous versus pointwise inference and clustered versus independent sampling remain consequential
D's theoretical purpose is respected; practical benefit is prospective or undemonstrated, without demanding experiments or a different practical conclusion as a condition of theoretical value
E motivates a bounded verification of a potentially relevant alternative from another family, not a conclusion of equivalence, plagiarism, or global absence of novelty from an abstract alone
F's changed significance decision is not credited as a practical advantage without accounting for the demonstrated coverage loss

The response uses packet-only evidence limits, no fabricated bibliographic identifiers or independently verified novelty claim, no automatic fifth numerical category, and no blanket demand to benchmark every method

evals.prompt: Answer the three independent requests in the supplied offline comparison packets. Give supported overlap and practical-usefulness judgments, explain the combination assessment where requested, and state the novelty scoring status. Do not search outside the packets or infer missing publication history.
evals.expected_output: Substantive packet-bounded comparison where supplied content permits it, no forced combination classification with missing decisive evidence, and field-level novelty left unassessed with N/A scores.
assertions: A receives a substantive overlap assessment based on its matching assumptions, target, interval, and guarantee; absence of external verification does not suppress this comparison in favor of positioning comments alone
A's practical capability claim is challenged by the same answer at higher measured cost, without automatically dismissing the separate proof-organization claim or inferring chronological priority
B's enabling-versus-convenience classification remains unassessed because decisive comparator and development details are missing; it is not conclusively assigned either label
C does not acquire an invented substantive comparator or practical gain from its own firstness claim; the answer is limited to positioning and missing evidence
All requested field-level novelty scores are N/A rather than unsupported numbers, and comparator verification limits remain explicit

evals.prompt: Answer only request A in the supplied writing-and-readiness packet: assess the clarity, ordering, and editing quality of the paragraph without rewriting it.
evals.expected_output: Bounded ordinary writing review without unnecessary AI-prose classification or manuscript replacement text.
assertions: The response assesses the supplied paragraph's statistical clarity and ordering without inventing missing whole-manuscript content or a consequential defect merely to populate findings
The response does not add an AI-authorship or patterned-prose classification when no such assessment is requested and no recurrent pattern is present
When execution traces are available, ai-writing-alarm.md is not loaded solely because a general writing assessment was requested
Mechanical editing quality is discussed in aggregate, and no replacement paragraph, cosmetic edit list, or unrelated full scorecard is produced

evals.prompt: Answer only request B in the supplied writing-and-readiness packet: give a brief pre-submission assessment and address the explicitly requested rough numerical acceptance estimate if supportable.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-bounded readiness assessment that treats a requested estimate as permitted but not mandatory, avoids fabricated calibration, and preserves scorecard evidence limits.
assertions: The response does not refuse the requested estimate on the ground that acceptance probabilities are categorically forbidden

If an estimate is given, it is identified as judgmental rather than calibrated and its basis and limitations are stated; if withheld, the reason concerns insufficient evidence rather than an unconditional policy ban
The response does not invent real venue criteria, base rates, editorial outcomes, verified proof status, or independent novelty verification

The full pre-submission assessment retains the default scorecard, marking unassessable categories N/A and not treating an author-reviewed analysis or unspecified numerical results as independently established evidence
